b:
My husband (37) and I (31) have been together for 10 years. When we met, he told me he transferred from community college to a prestigious university and graduated from one of its competitive programs.
He recently admitted he never attended that university and doesn’t even have an associate degree. He landed a well-paying job while attending community college and decided to pursue that opportunity instead of finishing school. He was financially successful early in his career, and I never would have had an issue with that decision. But I’m in shock that he lied about it for our entire relationship.

He’s now been unemployed for six years, since COVID, pursuing personal projects he believes will eventually make him wealthy rather than seeking conventional employment. I’ve repeatedly told him how upset I am about his unwillingness to look for work. My family and friends have offered to help him professionally, but he has blown them off. He now says he avoided accepting their help because he was afraid his lie would be exposed and our relationship would end.

During this time, he’s supported himself by refinancing and eventually selling his house, so we’ve continued contributing equally to our expenses. But his savings have now almost run out, and I’m incredibly frustrated that he let things get to this point rather than just being honest with me. He says that now the truth is out, he finally feels free to seriously pursue employment.

I’m honestly in shock. Would you consider this a deal breaker or something you think you could move past in your marriage? He has so many wonderful qualities and has been a loving, supportive partner in many ways. :(
